title: From the Editor — What Jessie Left
settingText: Glasshouse courtyard in late-day light, with open doors, old glass panels, travel gear near a wall and the road visible beyond. The image should suggest a place someone once knew well without revealing who recognizes whom.
summary: Art-directed opening editorial splash for Sunforge Outlaw Issue 11. Entice the reader, establish the live pressure and world feeling, and preserve the story page-one reveal.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-PAGE ART-DIRECTED SPLASH. Use one cinematic illustration rather than sequential panels. Reserve a large, deliberately quiet field for the supplied editorial body copy. The illustration supports the text without depicting the next issue's reveal literally.

LETTERING LAYOUT. Treat the supplied CAPTION lines as designed editorial typography, not speech balloons: strong heading, readable body copy, generous leading and margins, and a prominent final hook line. Do not invent any additional text, logos, signage, credits or slogans.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: FROM THE EDITOR

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A wrong name can start a fight.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A right one can be worse.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: For months, Brandon has been the person strangers insist they know.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: At Glasshouse, somebody calls across the courtyard and gets a name exactly right.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Not Brandon’s.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Jessie’s.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Before the road, before Eva, before any of this, Jessie Petrescu had places where people knew when she would arrive, what she drank, and how long she was likely to stay.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: One of those people has just seen her again.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: This time, nobody can blame mistaken identity.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: — Jeff Hines

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Star Splitter Visions

title: Glasshouse
summary: The group reaches Glasshouse, a low settlement of shaded courtyards and salvaged translucent panels. Jessie recognizes the layout before she admits she knows the place.

panelPlan.text: Glasshouse appears in late light: low walls, open courtyards, old translucent panels used for shade and windbreak, gardens protected behind patched glazing.
Jessie slows before the main courtyard and takes a side approach without consulting a map.
Eva notices Jessie knows where the wash pump and guest yard are located.
Brandon notices Eva noticing and says nothing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You've been here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: A while ago.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Long enough to know the back entrance.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Long enough to know where people park badly.

title: Jessie Petrescu
summary: Rachael Hughes sees Jessie across the courtyard and calls her by her full name with genuine surprise. Jessie freezes harder at accurate recognition than Brandon usually does at false identity.

panelPlan.text: Rachael crosses a courtyard carrying folded cloth, glances toward the rig and stops.
Her face changes from recognition to disbelief before she calls out.
Jessie stops with one hand still on a cargo strap.
Eva looks reflexively toward Brandon, then realizes he has nothing to do with this event.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: Jessie Petrescu, you vanished.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: That was not the entrance I wanted.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Try not to look frightened.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I am considering driving away.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: You already did that once.

title: A Correct History
summary: Rachael establishes immediately that her recognition is real by recalling specific, mundane details of Jessie's time at Glasshouse that Jessie confirms reluctantly.

panelPlan.text: Rachael crosses the distance and checks Jessie with the familiar entitlement of an old friend rather than a stranger proving identity.
She recalls Jessie's old sleeping room, the place she parked the rig and the cup she refused to let anyone else use.
Jessie corrects small exaggerations rather than denying the history.
Brandon relaxes because for once accurate recognition belongs to someone else and is not dangerous.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: You still park crooked when you're tired.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: The courtyard is crooked.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: You used that excuse four years ago.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Four years?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Do not encourage her.

title: The Blue Cup
summary: Rachael takes immediate advantage of Eva's curiosity, resurrecting the story of Jessie's treasured blue cup and exposing how much ordinary domestic history Jessie left behind.

panelPlan.text: Rachael leads them through a kitchen courtyard and points to a shelf where one chipped blue cup still sits among ordinary dishes.
Jessie insists the cup was practical rather than sentimental.
Rachael recounts the day it cracked and Jessie's disproportionate anger.
Eva is delighted by evidence that Jessie once cared about a specific household object.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: She loved that cup.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I owned it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: You swore for ten minutes when it cracked.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: It was a good cup.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: This is the most domestic thing I know about you.

title: Four Months
summary: Eva learns Jessie lived at Glasshouse for four months, long enough to have a room, chores, routines and people who expected her at supper.

panelPlan.text: Rachael opens an old guest room now used for storage and points out where Jessie's cot once stood.
She recalls Jessie repairing pumps in exchange for lodging and taking a regular evening shift on a greenhouse vent system.
Jessie corrects Rachael's claim that she stayed eight months to four.
Rachael counters that Jessie complained for eight months' worth of time.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: You lived in this room eight months.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Four months.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: You complained for eight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You lived somewhere four months?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Do not make it sound medical.

title: A Person With Routines
summary: Glasshouse reveals a version of Jessie that is not fundamentally different, merely more settled: she still repaired things, complained efficiently and left early for work, but people knew where to find her every day.

panelPlan.text: Rachael points out the repair shed where Jessie used to work mornings.
A longtime resident remembers Jessie sleeping through breakfast after late repairs and confirms the routine without romanticizing it.
Brandon joins them carrying fuel filters and listens to the history with quiet interest.
Jessie grows less defensive once the stories stop sounding like evidence against her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: You worked the pumps before breakfast and the vents after supper.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: The pumps were quieter in the morning.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: You had a schedule.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I have schedules now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You had one that other people knew.

title: The Night She Left
summary: Rachael recounts Jessie's departure without dramatic embellishment: one evening the rig was packed, and by dawn Jessie was gone after telling only the person on night watch.

panelPlan.text: Jessie and Rachael walk alone through the vehicle yard after the others give them space.
Rachael points to the gate Jessie used and says the departure itself was orderly, not chaotic.
Jessie says she did tell someone she was leaving.
Rachael says telling the night watch is not the same as saying goodbye to people who expected breakfast with her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: You packed after supper and were gone before breakfast.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I told Marin on watch.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: Marin was not the person making breakfast for you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I did not know I owed everybody a ceremony.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: You owed some of us a sentence.

title: Supper
summary: At supper, Jessie's old relationships become visible as a network rather than one grievance. Several people are simply pleased to see her; Rachael's hurt does not define Glasshouse's entire memory of Jessie.

panelPlan.text: Long courtyard supper under old translucent panels. Jessie is greeted by several residents who remember repairs, arguments and shared meals.
One person is warmly delighted, another mildly annoyed she never returned a wrench, another barely remembers her.
Eva notices memory is distributed rather than unified.
Rachael lets the broader community claim parts of Jessie too instead of monopolizing the reunion.

dialogueInline.speaker: Resident
dialogueInline.text: You still owe me a wrench.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I gave that wrench back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: You gave back a different wrench.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: This place has records.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Mostly in Rachael.

title: You Leave Early
summary: After supper, Rachael names the grievance beneath the jokes: Jessie tends to leave relationships while they are still good, before anyone can ask what comes next.

panelPlan.text: Rachael and Jessie sit apart on low steps while the courtyard clears.
Rachael says Jessie did not leave after a fight, betrayal or failure; she left when staying began to look normal.
Jessie rejects the idea that leaving requires a catastrophe to justify it.
Rachael agrees, then points out that choosing departure does not erase the effect on people left behind.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: You leave while things are still good.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: That is a strange thing to hold against me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: I am not saying you needed a disaster to leave.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: I am saying you left before anyone could ask what staying meant to you.

title: Before They Depend
summary: Rachael sharpens the accusation without diagnosing Jessie: when other people begin planning around Jessie's presence, Jessie becomes restless and leaves before those expectations become obligations.

panelPlan.text: Rachael recalls the week people began talking about expanding the repair shed and naturally included Jessie in next year's work.
Jessie remembers the same conversations as a trap closing without anyone intentionally setting one.
Rachael says nobody demanded Jessie stay forever; they simply began relying on her continuing to be there.
Jessie admits that was enough to make the road feel suddenly necessary.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: The week we started planning next year's repairs, you packed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Everybody talked like next year had already been decided.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: Because you had been here four months.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: That does not sign the next twelve.

title: Chosen Departures
summary: Jessie admits the part she understands about herself without turning it into a grand explanation: she prefers departures she chooses to futures other people assume on her behalf.

panelPlan.text: Jessie watches the road through gaps in the courtyard wall while Rachael remains seated.
She says arriving somewhere always feels like a choice and staying eventually begins to feel like inertia.
Rachael asks whether leaving before anyone can disappoint her is part of it.
Jessie refuses certainty she does not have but admits she likes knowing the departure belongs to her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I don't like waking up and realizing everybody else has decided I live somewhere.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: You could tell them that before you pack.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I could have.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: You left instead.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I did.

title: Eva Can Stay
summary: Eva approaches, reads the seriousness correctly and offers to leave. Jessie asks her to stay, deliberately allowing a current relationship to witness an old one rather than keeping the two lives separate.

panelPlan.text: Eva approaches with three cups, slows when she sees the tone and offers to put them down and go.
Jessie asks her to stay before Rachael answers.
Rachael makes room on the step rather than turning Eva into an audience.
The three sit with a silence that does not require filler dialogue.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I can leave the cups and go.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Stay.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: You are part of the reason this conversation matters now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Then I will listen more than I talk.

title: Ask Jessie
summary: Later, Eva asks Brandon what he thinks happened between Jessie and Rachael. Brandon refuses to give her a theory that would turn Jessie's future words into evidence for his interpretation.

panelPlan.text: Eva finds Brandon outside washing dishes and repairing a split leather strap.
She asks whether he thinks Rachael is right about Jessie.
Brandon says he has several possibilities and keeps working.
When Eva asks for them, he explains why he will not supply a lens she might then impose on Jessie.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Do you think Rachael is right about her?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I have several ideas.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Which one do you believe?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: If I tell you, you will start listening to Jessie for proof of it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Then what am I supposed to do?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Ask Jessie.

title: If She Doesn't Answer
summary: Eva asks what happens if Jessie refuses to explain herself. Brandon treats refusal as a boundary rather than an investigative failure.

panelPlan.text: Eva sits on the workbench while Brandon threads the repaired strap.
She asks whether friendship entitles her to an answer about something that affects the group.
Brandon distinguishes asking from being owed.
Eva accepts that the question may remain partly unanswered even inside a close relationship.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: What if she doesn't answer?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then leave it there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Even if it matters to us?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: You can tell her why it matters. You still do not get to demand her history.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: That makes curiosity much less convenient.

title: Why Did You Leave
summary: Eva follows Brandon's advice and asks Jessie directly without offering theories first. Jessie chooses to answer while they walk a quiet side courtyard.

panelPlan.text: The next morning, Eva finds Jessie checking condensation channels beneath the old glass panels.
Eva states that Rachael's story made her wonder whether Jessie left because staying itself frightened her.
Then she withdraws the interpretation and asks the simpler question.
Jessie appreciates the correction enough to answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I started making theories about why you left.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I am shocked.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I stopped. Why did you leave?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Because staying had started becoming a life I had not chosen.

title: What Made Staying Wrong
summary: Jessie clarifies that nothing was wrong with Glasshouse. The pressure came from a good place becoming permanent through assumption rather than explicit choice.

panelPlan.text: Jessie and Eva walk past the old repair shed and guest room while Jessie answers in the setting itself.
Jessie says she liked Glasshouse and liked Rachael, which made the decision harder rather than easier.
The change came when ordinary conversations started placing Jessie in next year's plans without asking.
Eva understands why no single event exists to blame.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: What made staying feel wrong?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Nothing here was wrong.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I liked the work. I liked Rachael. Then everybody started talking about next year like I had already signed something.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: So you left before the assumption became an obligation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: That is close enough for today.

title: Rachael Was Right About Some Things
summary: Jessie gives Eva a partial answer rather than a self-diagnosis. Rachael accurately saw a pattern in Jessie's departures, but Jessie does not accept every motive Rachael attaches to it.

panelPlan.text: Eva asks whether that means Rachael was right.
Jessie distinguishes behavior from motive: she does leave when permanence starts being assumed, but she does not know whether that is fear, preference, habit or several things.
Eva resists pushing for one neat cause.
Jessie notices and appreciates the restraint without praising it explicitly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Rachael thinks you leave whenever people start assuming you will stay.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Rachael is allowed to be right about some things.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Do you know why you do it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Not well enough to give you a clean answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Then I will not turn the messy one into a theory.

title: Will You Leave Us
summary: Eva asks the question underneath her curiosity: whether Jessie will eventually disappear from Brandon and Eva the way she left Glasshouse. Jessie refuses to promise a permanence she does not know she can offer.

panelPlan.text: Eva stops walking near the courtyard gate, making the question direct rather than casual.
She asks whether Jessie expects to leave the group once traveling together feels too much like a life.
Jessie does not comfort Eva with a false promise.
She says she is here now because she keeps choosing to be, which is the most honest assurance she can give.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Will you do it to us?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I don't know.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: That is a terrible answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: It is the honest one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I am here today because I chose to stay after yesterday. I can promise that much.

title: The Packed Rig
summary: By late afternoon the rig is fully packed for departure. Nothing is keeping the group at Glasshouse: no crisis, broken vehicle or unresolved mystery.

panelPlan.text: Jessie secures the final strap on a completely road-ready rig.
Raina and Samuel have their own packs ready. Brandon fills water. Eva returns borrowed bedding.
Rachael watches without trying to manufacture a reason for Jessie to stay.
The open road is visible through the gate, making departure genuinely available.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: You still pack before anybody can argue.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Packing is not leaving.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: That is new.

title: Supper Invitation
summary: Rachael invites Jessie to one family supper without making it a test of friendship or asking for a future promise. Jessie initially defaults to the road schedule.

panelPlan.text: Rachael stands beside the packed rig and invites the whole group to one more family supper.
Jessie looks automatically toward the lowering sun and calculates the next stop.
She says they can still reach the next shelter before dark.
Rachael accepts the refusal without guilt or argument, changing the emotional terms of the choice.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: Since nobody is fighting and nothing is broken, stay for supper.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: We can make the next stop before dark.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: Then you can go. I am inviting you, not scheduling you.

title: Do You Want To Stay
summary: Brandon interrupts Jessie's automatic logistical answer with the one question the issue has been circling: does she want to stay tonight.

panelPlan.text: Jessie reaches for the driver's side after Rachael steps away.
Brandon does not argue for either departure or staying; he asks Jessie what she wants.
Eva remains silent, resisting the impulse to answer for the group.
Jessie looks from the road to the courtyard and makes the choice without pressure from either direction.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Do you want to stay?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: One night.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then we leave tomorrow.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I can unpack the bedding.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Only the bedding.

title: One More Night
summary: Jessie carries one bag back inside and stays because remaining is voluntary too. The issue closes on supper rather than departure, with no promise about next month or next year.

panelPlan.text: Jessie unfastens one small bag from the packed rig and carries it back through the courtyard gate.
Rachael notices but does not comment on the symbolic weight of the act.
At family supper, Jessie occupies an ordinary seat between old and current companions.
Final panel: the packed rig remains visible outside, ready for tomorrow, while Jessie stays inside tonight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: There is stew.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: You always lead with the weakest argument.

dialogueInline.speaker: Rachael Hughes
dialogueInline.text: You stayed anyway.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: For supper.

title: Next: ALREADY WAITING
settingText: Hushwater at twilight. A weathered house waits beside the road. Inside a window, a sealed packet sits on a table beside an old ledger. No visible name, no person waiting in frame.
summary: Art-directed closing teaser splash for Sunforge Outlaw Issue 11. Point directly at the next loaded pressure without revealing its resolution.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Jessie stayed one more night because she wanted to.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Then the road opens again.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: At Hushwater, a house has been waiting since winter.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: There is a packet inside.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: There is a name on it.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Raina has been with Brandon for months.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Samuel has too.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Neither of them could have arrived first.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Somebody did.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: NEXT: ALREADY WAITING
